title: The Success Habit
coreMove: Make leverage-seeking a repeated habit so decisions keep narrowing before busyness takes over.
sourcePressure: Part 2 turns the Focusing Question into a repeated success habit, centered on asking for leverage often enough that it changes decisions.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating habit as routine for its own sake or repeating generic habit advice.

hook: A single choice changes the whole day
The real priority is hiding under the busy work
The Success Habit as a generic focus opener
counterintuition: Focus is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: Set a timer and list priorities
Write down your one thing without a concrete context
examples: generic office worker choosing email or strategy

exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she adds one leverage question to the 8:45 queue review and changes the first staffing move before calls flood in
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a headset row with one queue monitor glowing at 8:45 a.m.

exampleSpecs.stakes: actors receive too many notes to improve
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before every rehearsal she asks which one note would make the scene easier for everyone and cuts the rest from the call sheet
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a marked script beside a call sheet with five crossed-out notes

exampleSpecs.stakes: weak colonies can be missed among routine checks
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: at each truck stop he asks which hive condition would make tomorrow's losses easier to prevent and opens that box first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a hive tool resting on a truck tailgate beside numbered colony cards

exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she uses the question at the top of the budget meeting and assigns the records request before chasing three smaller clips
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a newsroom budget board with one records request underlined

exampleSpecs.stakes: patients leave with too many exercises
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he builds a habit of asking which one movement makes the home program easier and removes three nice-to-have drills
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a resistance band looped around a discharge packet on a treatment table

exampleSpecs.stakes: books stall between copyedit and proof
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she realizes the habit worked only after she asked the leverage question at every Friday handoff instead of during crises
exampleSpecs.firstImage: proof pages stacked beside a Friday handoff checklist

skillTargets: attach the focusing question to recurring moments

tryThisNowSpec: Attach the leverage question to one daily trigger you already meet, such as opening your calendar, clearing a tray, or starting a shift.
